text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: WBC 6,500 /μL, Hemoglobin 12.1 g/dL, Platelets 280,000 /μL (normal). Peripheral_Blood_Smear: No clumping of platelets observed, normal morphology of other cells.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the platelet count is normal, I need to assess for a coagulation factor deficiency. Has there been any history of joint bleeding or prolonged bleeding after dental work or circumcision?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Frequent epistaxis. I also have Mucous membrane bleeding, Diffuse petechiae on distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal platelet count and smear but persistent mucocutaneous bleeding, I suspect a platelet function defect like von Willebrand disease. Is there a family history of easy bruising or bleeding disorders in your relatives?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical issues. Up-to-date on vaccinations. Social history: Attends preschool. Lives with parents and one older sibling.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Bleeding_Time
REQUEST TEST: von_Willebrand_Factor_Antigen

speaker: Doctor
text: Since von Willebrand factor is normal but bleeding time is prolonged, this points toward a specific platelet function defect. Have you noticed if the bleeding worsens when the child is ill or febrish, and does the child take aspirin or NSAIDs regularly?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies any fever, significant weight loss, joint pains, or recent infections.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Platelet_Function_Assay
REQUEST TEST: Glanzman_Thrombasthenia_Screening

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Platelet_Function_Assay: Abnormal platelet aggregation in response to all agonists except ristocetin. Glanzman_Thrombasthenia_Screening: Positive (ELISA Binding Assay shows Platelet surfaces deficient in GIIb/IIIa receptors).

speaker: Doctor
text: The positive Glanzmann screening and abnormal aggregation pattern confirm Glanzmann thrombasthenia, a platelet function disorder. DIAGNOSIS READY: Glanzmann thrombasthenia
